attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated as his position.

semantics.note: Matches the words. It is a firm present-tense claim about measurability, so observation is correct, though the line is rhetorical in tone.

contract.note: The contract reads the line as literal impossibility and counts after-the-fact API bills as measured task cost. In context, an informed reader would take it as companies lacking practical visibility and predictability of spend and returns. The retrospective-vs-predictive choice and the May 2026 window were the evaluator's, not the speaker's. Scoring on this reading is stretched against him.

evidence.note: Dated May 2026 benchmark logging API cost per task for three bug fixes. The operator also sells an evaluated product. It shows API spend can be logged in a controlled harness, not that businesses can measure full task cost or ROI.
A user report that cost is shown per trace but session totals don't add up. It is anecdotal context about spend visibility and settles neither component.
Its economic model rests on assumed redeployment of time saved, so it is projected, not realised, ROI. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The contract's literal-impossibility reading is unfair to the speaker. Under the fair reading (practical inability to measure task cost and ROI), the packet has no evidence that settles it. One vendor-adjacent benchmark logging API costs and an assumption-based ROI model do not establish or refute the claim. Under the contract's own terms the cost part would fall to e1 and the ROI part would stay open, but that turns on an interpretation the speaker did not supply.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: A claim of necessary conditions for meeting the industry's projections and commitments. The antecedent comes from the preceding sentence and is kept. It reads as much like analysis as forecast, but conditional framing is acceptable.

contract.note: Taking the 2030 endpoint from the nearby 'four years' wording is reasonable. Growth metric, profitability basis and financing scope are unspecified, so any scoring would depend on evaluator definitions. The contract correctly refuses to treat the requirements merely occurring together as proof that they were necessary.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of an expanded multiyear AWS commitment. It shows a commitment exists, not that it has been fulfilled or what fulfilling it requires.
Anthropic's own disclosure of Amazon investment and growth in run-rate revenue. It does not establish what financing or profitability the commitments require.
OpenAI's own announcement of $122B in committed capital before the post. It does not settle future financing needs or the other components.
Anthropic's S-1 risk factor on uncertain compute needs. No decisive event and no fulfillment of the antecedent.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent (the commitments being fulfilled) has not occurred by the evaluation date, and the provisional deadline is June 2030. No early-resolution event shows the commitments being fulfilled without one of the asserted requirements. All evidence items are company disclosures and context only, so the conditional cannot be scored yet.
